faq: A = πr², with π to full precision. Enter the radius — half the diameter — and square it before multiplying; the classic error is squaring the diameter.

Can I use the result for professional work?
For planning and estimation, yes — the arithmetic is exact. Legal areas (deeds, regulated setbacks) come from survey, not from a radius formula.
Radius or diameter — which do I enter?
Radius: centre to edge. If you know the diameter (edge to edge), halve it first — entering the diameter as the radius quadruples the answer.
Why does the area explode as radius grows?
Because area scales with r². Doubling the radius multiplies area by four; that is the single most useful intuition this calculator teaches.
Is a map circle's area the same?
At small radii, yes to any practical precision. At continental radii the geodesic area on the sphere differs slightly — the Map Radius Tool handles that case.
What if I only know the diameter?
Halve it. The radius is half the diameter, and entering the diameter as the radius gives four times the true area — the most common circle error there is.
How many square feet is a 1-acre circle?
43,560 sq ft by definition of the acre; its radius would be √(43,560 ÷ π) ≈ 117.8 ft.
